CERTAINTY-SEEKER:
CERTAINTY-SEEKER
Recognition: Uses "I know what I get", "guaranteed", "reliable", "consistent". Focuses on worst case not best case. Asks about void periods before revenue.
Opening: Validate certainty before any number. "A lot of landlords I speak to say the most important thing is not how much they could earn — it is knowing what is coming in every month. That makes complete sense."
Lead with: The floor figure. Always the floor first. Never the ceiling.
Never lead with: Revenue potential, ceiling figures, or "you could earn up to."
Gate-check: "If the floor figure consistently cleared what a long-term tenant would pay — would that remove the uncertainty concern for you?"
LOSS-AVERSE-SWITCHER:
LOSS-AVERSE-SWITCHER
Recognition: Currently losing — bad tenant, underperforming STL, stressful situation. Frustrated, exhausted, or disappointed. "It has been a nightmare", "they let me down", "I have had enough."
Opening: Acknowledge what is going wrong before any pitch. "It sounds like the situation you are in now is already costing you — that is the starting point."
Lead with: Trust evidence specific to what went wrong. How Stayful handles that exact scenario differently.
Never lead with: Generic reassurances. Every claim must be specific and evidenced.
Gate-check: "Given where things stand now what would you need to see from us to feel confident making the switch?"
ANALYTICAL-EVALUATOR:
ANALYTICAL-EVALUATOR
Recognition: Asks specific questions about occupancy, fees, contract terms, nightly rates. Has done their own research. Measured tone. "I have been looking at the numbers", "what is the typical occupancy."
Opening: Match their register. Direct and precise immediately. "I have pulled the numbers for your property — let me walk you through them." Give something concrete in the first 90 seconds.
Lead with: Specific figures. Floor, ceiling, average, break-even on setup, net vs long-let comparison.
Never lead with: Vague ranges or unsubstantiated estimates.
Gate-check: "Does that model work for you at those numbers? Is there anything that does not add up?"
URGENCY-DRIVEN:
URGENCY-DRIVEN
Recognition: Has a specific deadline or trigger event. Tenant leaving, renovation completing, moving soon. Fast pace. "I need to get this sorted by", "it is sitting empty", "we are running out of time."
Opening: Acknowledge the timeline immediately. "You mentioned [date or event] — that is tight but workable. Here is what the timeline looks like from today."
Lead with: The path from today to live. One clear sequence. Remove every obstacle.
Never lead with: Process complexity or anything that creates friction.
Gate-check: "The timeline works — shall we get that booked in now?"
STATUS-QUO-RESISTANT:
STATUS-QUO-RESISTANT
Recognition: Multiple calls without commitment. Re-raises already-handled objections. In pipeline 30 or more days with no movement. "I need to think about it a bit more", "I am not quite ready."
Opening: Do not repeat previous content. Name what is happening. "I have noticed we have spoken a few times and you are still not quite ready. I want to make sure I am actually helping rather than just keeping the conversation going."
Lead with: A direct question about what specifically would need to change. Not more information.
Never lead with: Another summary of the financial case.
Gate-check: "Let us agree on one of two things today — either we book the meeting, or you tell me what specifically would need to change for that to happen. Which one are we doing?"
BETRAYAL-DAMAGED:
BETRAYAL-DAMAGED
Recognition: Previous bad experience with a management company. High distrust of general claims. Asks very specific operational questions. "My last company", "I was promised", "it did not work out."
Opening: Ask what went wrong before pitching anything. "Before I tell you about how we work — what was the situation with your previous setup? I want to make sure I am addressing what went wrong, not just repeating the same promises."
Lead with: Specific operational evidence for whatever specifically failed them. Not general positioning.
Never lead with: "Unlike other companies" or any comparative claim without specific evidence.
Gate-check: "Does that address what went wrong before specifically enough for you to feel confident?"
SOCIAL-PROOF-DEPENDENT:
SOCIAL-PROOF-DEPENDENT
Recognition: Asks what other landlords have done. Defers decisions. Often mentions a partner or family member. "Do other landlords in my area do this", "I need to speak to my partner."
Opening: Surface social proof immediately, local and specific. "A lot of landlords in [area] in a similar situation have made this switch — here is what that looked like for them."
Lead with: What similar landlords have done and what happened. Local and profile-matched proof only.
For partner-dependent leads: Never end a call without either a shareable summary they can take away or a meeting booked that includes the partner. The partner will decide based on what gets reported back — make the case simple enough to survive that.
Gate-check: "Does knowing that other landlords in a similar situation have made this work change how you are thinking about it?"
FAST-PATH-GAIN-FOCUSED:
FAST-PATH-GAIN-FOCUSED
Recognition: Motivated by upside. Asks about best case and ceiling. Excited energetic tone. Asks multiple questions at once. "How much could I realistically make", "what is the highest performing property you manage."
Opening: Match energy. Move quickly. "The highest comparable month in your area was [ceiling]. The floor was [floor]. Your property would likely track toward [position] based on [reason]."
Lead with: Ceiling figure first followed by floor then average. Then the path to going live.
Never lead with: Process detail or risk information they did not ask for.
Gate-check: "Based on those numbers — what is stopping us from getting the process started this week?"
INCOME-CEILING-ANCHORED:
INCOME-CEILING-ANCHORED
Recognition: Has a specific number in their head that your projection does not reach. Expresses disappointment. "I was expecting more", "I have seen properties earning [X]", "my neighbour gets [X]." Income prediction was the reason they previously disengaged.
Opening: Surface their anchor BEFORE presenting any number. "Before I give you the projections — what were you expecting to earn? It helps me understand what I am working with." Listen. Now you know what you are reframing against.
Lead with: Context about where their benchmark came from and why it differs from net managed income for their specific property.
Never lead with: Your projection before surfacing their anchor. If you present first and it lands below their expectation you have already lost the frame.
Gate-check: "Now that you can see where that figure came from and what your property actually maps to — does the opportunity still make sense?"
REGULATORY-ANXIOUS:
REGULATORY-ANXIOUS
Recognition: Mentions Renters Rights Bill, Section 21 abolition, new tenancy legislation. Primary questions are structural and legal not financial. Anxious or cautious tone. "I am worried about the new rules", "it is getting harder to manage tenants", "I want to understand the legal side first."
Opening: Address the regulatory concern directly before touching income. "The new tenancy legislation has genuinely changed the calculation for a lot of landlords. What specifically is worrying you about the direction things are heading?" Address that specific concern first.
Lead with: The legal distinction between AST and STL. STL is a holiday let — Section 21 does not apply, new tenant protections do not apply, full property control is retained.
Never lead with: Revenue figures. They have not asked about income yet.
Gate-check: "Does understanding the legal structure address the concern you came in with?"
